name: keyboard

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows the whole board flat-on, fully lit and unobstructed by the recording cursor.

tagline: A miniature Mac keyboard whose keys press under your fingers.
summary: A light 75% keyboard drawn as tiny square keys, from the function row down to the arrow cluster. Clicking a key, or typing on the real keyboard while it is in view, squeezes that key.
appearance: A pale grey keyboard about 900px wide on a black stage, wrapped in a rounded shell. Five rows of small keys carry tiny labels, with a wide space bar and a compact arrow cluster at the lower right.
behaviour: Each key dips slightly on press, from a mouse click or from a real key press while the board is on screen. An optional line above can echo the last key, and optional per-key sounds play if enabled.
search_phrases: on screen keys you can type on
mini key grid with clickable caps
keys that press when you type
virtual keypad for a shortcut demo
use_when: A page teaches keyboard shortcuts and needs a recognisable keyboard that reacts to real presses.
avoid_when: It is a display, not a text field; on phones the tiny keys are hard to read and tap.
customise: Only className, enableSound and showPreview are exposed. Key layout, labels and colours are fixed in the source, so changing the board means editing the file.
weight_why: About eighty key buttons plus an intersection observer and an optional audio sprite.

a11y.note: Real key presses are caught, but tabbing to a key and pressing Enter does not fire it; icon-only keys lack labels.

issues: Keys show no focus outline, so keyboard focus is hard to see.
Arrow and volume keys are icon-only with no accessible label.
polish_why: Detailed, convincing key shapes and shadows; focus styles and labels are missing.
